title: Chain appends and skip nulls

blocks.text: `append` returns the builder itself, so calls chain: `sb.append("a").append("b")`. And `append` never refuses a `null` reference: it adds the four letters `"null"`. A value that may be `null` is checked before it is appended. `toString()` turns the finished builder into a String.
Write `trail(String... parts)` in `Breadcrumbs`. It returns the parts separated by `" / "`, leaving out every `null` part:

cases.says: trail("Home", null, "Java") is "Home / Java", with no "null" in it.
trail(null, "Docs") is "Docs", with no separator before it.

concepts: Appending a null reference adds the text "null", so a value that may be null is checked first.
append returns the builder itself, so calls chain, and toString() gives the finished String.
